cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Safe dance practice protects dancers from injury and supports long-term health and performance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: A warm-up gradually raises the heart rate, increases blood flow to muscles and prepares the body for dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: An effective warm-up includes pulse-raising activities, joint mobilisation, dynamic stretching and dance-specific movements

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: A cool-down gradually returns the body to a resting state and helps prevent stiffness and soreness

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Cool-down should include gentle movement to lower the heart rate and static stretches to maintain flexibility

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Injury prevention involves wearing appropriate footwear, using suitable flooring and following correct technique

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Dancers should understand common dance injuries such as sprains, strains and stress fractures and their causes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Nutrition supports energy, recovery and bone health — dancers need balanced meals with carbohydrates, protein and hydration

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Dehydration affects concentration, coordination and performance quality, so regular fluid intake is essential

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: Safe rehearsal means taking rest breaks, not training through pain and building intensity gradually

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: The dance environment must be safe: well-ventilated, with sprung floors, adequate lighting and clear space

cards.front: Recall a key point about Safe Dance Practice
cards.back: AQA 8236 expects students to understand safe practice as part of the performance and health context

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — safe dance practice?
cards.back: 1. For Safe Dance Practice questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Safe Dance Practice 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
Explain why warm-up and cool-down are essential parts of safe dance practice. Give specific examples for each. [6 marks]

AO1 (Performance): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of safe dance practice, including choreographic processes, performing skills and dance appreciation relevant to AQA 8236. AO2 (Choreography): Apply knowledge and understanding of safe dance practice through the creative process of choreography, selecting and using movement material and choreographic devices.
